title: Field seller heuristics — quirky lab notes (draft)
body:
Purpose: quick, low-friction heuristics for sellers to improvise when pilots get weird. This is intentionally informal — pocketable lines, micro‑scripts, decision shortcuts and last-minute triage steps. Treat as a lab notebook; we’ll extract clean cards after a few more field trials.

Context and assumptions:
- Audience: SEs, field sellers, solution architects running 1–3 week pilots.
- Goal: keep pilot momentum, limit escalation to Engineering, and preserve economics.
- Not for legal/contract negotiations; route to Legal if procurement > $100k ARR or data residency exceptions.

Quick opening script (30s):
- "We usually start with a tiny scope to prove latency and quality in your environment. If we hit a perf snag, we have three fallbacks we can move to immediately without reconfiguring infra."
- Hand two options: (A) lighter model + caching, (B) reserved capacity for burst windows.

3-minute triage checklist (on-call friendly):
1) Confirm SLO anchor: target P50/P95 and max tokens per request.
2) Ask: did request shape change? (longer prompts, different user flows)
3) Check routing: are requests hitting hosted vs. private?
4) Toggle (if available): enable prefix cache + micro-batching.
5) Offer immediate mitigation: switch to compatible quantized variant for 10–30m to buy time.

Micro-scripts for common objections:
- "Cost is unpredictable" -> "We can pin model variants and use a simple prefix cache; I’ll show a per-token dashboard and an estimate for your typical session in 10 minutes."
- "Latency spikes" -> "Two quick knobs: reduce max_tokens, or route critical paths to reserved capacity. Which matters more to you: reliability or throughput?"
- "Security/regulatory" -> "We can demo a VPC private control-plane flow in a sandbox; it typically adds 2–3 weeks for SOC/Paperwork but minimal runtime change."

Pilot starter template (seller checklist):
- Confirm three business signals to measure success (e.g., conversion uplift, average handling time, reroute rate).
- Define representative prompt set (max 50 samples) and a worst-case noisy example set (10 samples).
- Baseline: record P50/P95 latency, token cost per call, and hallucination rate on 50 inputs.
- Set auto-fallback policy: model A -> model B -> degrade to cached response after N failures.

Fallback knob cheatsheet (what to flip fast):
- Model quantization: move to 8-bit variant (cost down, slight quality delta).
- Batching window: expand from 50ms to 150ms for cheaper throughput (only if customer tolerates small tail increase).
- Route critical flows to reserved capacity during predicted office hours.
- Prefix caching: cache the first 1–2 turns for multi-turn flows.

Stakeholder one-liners (for CTTO/CFO/PM):
- CTO: "We can run a private control-plane POC in a week to validate network policy; runtime is identical."
- CFO: "Pinned variants + usage alerts let us cap monthly spend and run automated throttles."
- PM: "We’ll ship a 2% lift experiment in week 3 using the same model; if quality drops we’ll fallback automatically."

Edge-case vignettes (real field examples):
1) Fintech: customer had intermittent 500s during batch reconciliation — quick fix was a routing rule to isolate heavy analytic jobs to dedicated nodes (reduced 95th by 40%).
2) Marketplace search: longer prompts from sellers broke batching heuristics; solution was to set a per-route max_input_tokens and pre-truncate older context.

Metrics to show in a quick deck slide (single-slide):
- Baseline vs. mitigated (P95 latency, per-call cost, success rate) measured over 48h.
- Pilot win criteria: >10% reduction in handling time or >2% conversion uplift.

Rapid roleplay prompts (for SE prep, 5m practice):
- Role A (buyer): "Latency is killing our demo. We can’t present with timeouts."
- Role B (seller): practice the 3-minute triage and offer the two immediate mitigations.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Test a one‑click demo flow that flips to cached responses without user-visible errors (engineers: GH PR linked above).
- Create a single-page PDF (for reps) with the triage checklist and two scripts.
- Collect 10 more real pilot vignettes and quantify impact of each fallback.

Concise escalation guide (if checklist fails):
- Capture logs/trace link, sample prompt that fails, and tenant ID. Create JIRA GTMSUP-# with tag "pilot-severe". Alert SRE on-call with subject: "Pilot outage: <account> — P95>target x3".

Notes to self (quirky, but useful):
- Use physical index cards in belt for field kits (yes this is analog but works in booth demos).
- Try a microdeck of bright yellow 3x5 cards with one-liners pinned to laptop.

References: links above; also see: "pilot-ops-fastlane-cheat-sheet-compact-draft.json" for handoff templates and "deployment-choice-decision-grid-sales-lab-wip.json" for decision matrices.

End: please comment inline with any examples you’ve used and any one-liners that actually closed a pilot. Will collate into final 2-pager for Q2 enablement.
